description: Every game system the mashup touches.

code.desc: Where the code lives ('-' = not started).

rows.description: Start the player's own Terraria.exe from {game} inside our process, apply our Harmony patches, then run Terraria's normal entry point. Game files are never changed.

_unverified.description: confirm Terraria.exe is x86 .NET Framework 4 + XNA, its entry point, and Steam start-up when launched by us

rows.description: Read sprites, sprite animations and translations straight from the player's Noita data.wak (read-only).

_unverified.description: data.wak layout is from community docs; confirm on the player's file

rows.description: Generated definitions from the sheets (EnemyDef, AttackDef, ...).

Vanilla Terraria has a fixed list of NPC types, so each Noita enemy rides on one vanilla 'carrier' NPC slot; a side table keyed by NPC index says which Noita enemy it is, and our patches replace that slot's AI, drawing, name, hit effects and loot.

_unverified.description: pick the carrier NPC/projectile types from the decompile: types with the fewest special cases

rows.description: Each spawn attempt, roll the Noita enemies whose zone matches the spawn tile and player, weighted by tier.
One state machine per AI archetype, written against a small body/world interface so it is unit-tested without the game.
Enemy shots ride on a vanilla carrier projectile the same way NPCs do.
Noita damage types and per-enemy multipliers applied to hits on our enemies.
Noita-style gold (coins by health), hearts and mana stars.
Debug keys to spawn any Noita enemy near the player and log what happens, for repeatable in-game tests and screenshots.
Stage 2: disturbed blocks fall, burn, melt and explode; untouched caves, islands and clouds stay put.
Stage 3: four wand slots next to the Terraria inventory, Noita spell editing.
Stage 3: Noita spells cast from wands; reuses the projectiles sheet.
Stage 4: four flask/item slots, flasks and Noita items.
